name: Silvery Spinnerets
summary: Near Wellspring Lake, Silvery Spinnerets are harvested from Lady Sathrah in northern Teldrassil. Her silver webs once gathered healing evening dew for the Temple of the Moon. The Sisterhood of Elune seeks the spinnerets for a sacred rite honoring her soul.

sections.title: Sacred Webbing and Corruption
sections.body: Lady Sathrah once spun shimmering webs by moonlight near Wellspring Lake. Her silver silk gathered evening mist into healing dew prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. But corruption reached her in Teldrassil, driving her into violent madness. Sathrah threatened her brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end her suffering and recover her spinnerets, bringing mercy to a once-revered creature of the great boughs.

sections.title: A Sacrifice for Rebirth
sections.body: The Sisterhood offers the recovered spinnerets to Elune at the central fountain inside the Temple of the Moon. In a rite called Sathrah's Sacrifice, the priestesses pray that the Moon Goddess will receive the creature's spirit, cleanse the madness that claimed her mortal body, and grant her peace in rebirth.

faq.q: Where do you get the Silvery Spinnerets?
faq.answer: Retrieve them from Lady Sathrah, a large spider along Teldrassil's northern borders near Wellspring Lake.

faq.q: Why does Priestess A'moora want the spinnerets?
faq.answer: Priestess A'moora seeks to offer the spinnerets to Elune as a sacred sacrifice. The rite honors Lady Sathrah's former purity and asks the goddess to cleanse her spirit and grant her peace and rebirth.

faq.q: Why were Lady Sathrah's webs special?
faq.answer: Lady Sathrah spun luminous silver silk that caught evening mist beneath the moonlight. The gathered dew held potent restorative magic and was prized by the Sisterhood of Elune, who stored it in the Temple of the Moon for healing.

faq.q: Why was Lady Sathrah killed if she was sacred?
faq.answer: Corruption drove Lady Sathrah into incurable madness alongside other wildlife in Teldrassil. Her aggression endangered the forest and threatened her brood, so the priestesses judged slaying her a sorrowful act of mercy.

angles.text: Lady Sathrah's tragic end reminds the Kaldorei that even creatures beloved by Elune can fall to the affliction sickening Teldrassil.
For servants of Elune, retrieving the spinnerets is a sacred funeral rite. It asks the Mother Moon to redeem a creature, rather than treating her death as mere extermination.
